walkthroughs.body_html:
Cathode (negative): cations reduced.

Cu^2+ + 2e- -> Cu.

Anode (positive): anions oxidised.

Brine = aq NaCl. Cathode: H2; anode: Cl2; solution: NaOH.

Used to make bleach, PVC and soaps.

Fe in Haber process, V2O5 in Contact process.

TM compounds colour glass and ceramics.

mcqs.q: Cathode product when electrolysing copper sulfate solution?
options: O2
Cu
SO4
H2

mcqs.q: Brine electrolysis produces all of these EXCEPT:
options: chlorine
hydrogen
sodium hydroxide
oxygen

mcqs.q: What happens to electrons when sodium reacts with chlorine?
options: Sodium loses one electron to chlorine; the resulting Na+ and Cl- ions attract electrostatically.
Sodium and chlorine share an electron between them.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.

mcqs.q: At which electrode are positive ions reduced during electrolysis?
options: Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
Positive ions are reduced at the anode because that's where positive things go.
At the cathode (the negative electrode) — positive ions gain electrons there.
Positive ions are oxidised at the cathode by losing protons.

mcqs.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
Positive ions are oxidised at the cathode by losing protons.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.
